title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Drawing, Expiry and Refund of Prepaid Hours
content:
### Terms no longer in force

Two terms of this basis are no longer in force. They stand here as a record of how blocks bought and
drawn under the older basis were treated:

> Where the tier sells blocks, prepaid hours are bought in multiples of the tier's minimum purchase at the tier's block rate, and they are drawn down by the labor hours of each completed call, oldest block first.

> Once the remaining block reaches zero the further hours of that call and of every later call are billed at the tier's overage rate until a new block is bought.

### Terms in force

**Face value on drawing.** Hours are drawn at their face value whatever band the work fell in, so an
after-hours call draws the hours worked and the after-hours premium alone is invoiced.

**Expiry.** Unused hours expire at the tier's expiry period counted forward in whole calendar months
from the day the block was bought, and expired hours are neither refunded nor restored.

**Rollover.** Where the tier allows rollover, hours unexpired at renewal carry into the next program
year; where it does not, they are forfeited at the year end.

**Refund on cancellation.** On cancellation the tier's refund portion of the unexpired unused hours is
refunded at the rate they were bought at, never at the current rate.

### Illustration of the expiry count (hypothetical)

On a program under the Demand Service Rate Programs whose expiry period is 12 calendar months, hours
bought on the tenth day of a month expire on the tenth day of the same month a year later, the count
running in whole calendar months from the day of purchase. Hours still unused on that day are neither
refunded nor restored, and the refund portion at cancellation reaches only hours that have not expired.

### Basis question

*A block bought at one rate is being refunded after the program's rates have risen.* The refund is taken
at the rate the hours were bought at, never at the current rate.
